messages:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: PAGE — tenant-routing-anomaly detected in dedicated pool dp-phi-21. Potential cross-tenant KV reads observed. Severity: P1. Affected customer: Peregrine Health (VPC, dedicated). See initial evidence below.

incident_bot: Log excerpt: `router: warn: ambiguous-prefix-match from proxy-7 on dp-phi-21; src-tenant=tid-998 -> matched-prefix=tid-112`

jess_prod_oncall: I'm on it. @omar_sre you up? I can start collection and a live mitigation if you want me to take the first 15.

omar_sre: I'm up. grabbing traces, will triage now. Lia, can you ping Peregrine and open a dedicated bridge? We should give them a short heads-up.

lia_support: On it — opening bridge and pinging their on-call (acm-poc). Messaging: "Seeing anomalous routing in your dedicated pool dp-phi-21. We're investigating possible cross-tenant reads. No confirmed data exfil yet. We'll update in 15."

jess_prod_oncall: Collection plan — I'm going to: 1) enable debug logging on proxy-7, 2) capture a 5 min pcap on the dataplane NIC, 3) snapshot KV access logs for dp-phi-21 from the last 10m. If we confirm cross-tenant reads, we evict suspect worker and failover to spare pool.

omar_sre: Running quick grep across recent proxy logs for ambiguous-prefix entries. snippet: ```
2026-03-15T13:04:11Z proxy-7 warn ambiguous-prefix-match tenant=tid-998 matched=tid-112 route=/models/enc-keys
2026-03-15T13:04:13Z proxy-7 info route-decide route=dedicated dp=dp-phi-21 selected_pool=default-dp-phi
```

ops_triage_lead: Jess — do not evict yet unless we have strong repro. Plan evicting will trigger warm-up and could impact throughput for Peregrine. Consider iptables blackhole for the suspect instance while we confirm.

eng_runtime_pm: Quick context — we pushed a small routing change to the dedicated route-resolver last night to improve prefix resolution performance (rollout id: rr-2026-03-14-81). It was targeted and should be safe but could interact with latebound tenant prefixes. If this is rd, we may need an immediate rollback to rr-2026-03-14-80.

omar_sre: Confirmed: the ambiguous-prefix entries spike at 13:04, coinciding with a topology update from the resolver. I'm attaching a sanitized mapping diff (redacted): ```
- prefix: 10ab.. -> tid-112
+ prefix: 10ab.. -> tid-998
```
This looks like a latebind edge-case where prefix overlap briefly pointed traffic to wrong tenant.

jess_prod_oncall: Lia — can you get Peregrine to check if they observed any partial responses or odd tokens in logs? Ask for any request ids around 13:04-13:07.

lia_support: Peregrine replied: they saw a handful of 200s with mismatched model ids in payloads. They exported request_ids: ["r_13A4f", "r_13A6b"]. They're asking if we rotated anything on their side.

omar_sre: Pulling telemetry for those request_ids now. Matching shows those requests served KV keys belonging to tid-112 but bearing tid-998 auth headers. That's consistent with misrouted reads. Need to determine scope (# keys, time window).

eng_runtime_pm: Given the rollback candidate is small and targeted, I recommend: 1) rollback resolver to rr-2026-03-14-80, 2) apply a transient prefix sanity check (reject overlapping binds for 60s), 3) start a slow canary to validate. This should restore correct prefix bindings quickly.

ops_triage_lead: +1 to rollback then canary. To reduce customer impact, do the rollback on a small set of hosts first (proxy-7 and proxy-9) and watch. If it fixes ambiguous-prefix logs we widen. Jess please coordinate throttle window.

jess_prod_oncall: Executing rollback on proxy-7 and proxy-9 now. Command: ```
kubectl -n infra set image deploy/route-resolver route-resolver=route-resolver:rr-2026-03-14-80 --record
```
Applying transient guard: ```
# deny binds when overlapping_prefix=true for 60s
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/guard/prefix_sanity -d '{"duration_s":60}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer *****'
```

incident_bot: rr-rollback action started by jess_prod_oncall.

omar_sre: After rollback, ambiguous-prefix logs drop immediately on proxy-7. First 3 min of post-rollback logs: ```
2026-03-15T13:07:02Z proxy-7 info prefix-bind tenant=tid-998 -> prefix=10ab..
2026-03-15T13:07:05Z proxy-7 info prefix-bind tenant=tid-112 -> prefix=10ac..
```
No further ambiguous-prefix entries.

lia_support: Peregrine confirms they no longer see mismatched responses as of 13:08. They appreciate the quick follow-up but request a root-cause note and timeline for their security team.

eng_runtime_pm: We'll prepare an RCA. Preliminary root cause: resolver rollout rr-2026-03-14-81 introduced a latebind ordering race with overlapping prefix updates, producing transient ambiguous-prefix matches. Mitigation: rollback + prefix-sanity guard. Longer-term: add deterministic resolution ordering and unit tests for overlapping binds.

ops_triage_lead: Action items (ownership):
- Omar: telemetry collection & evidence bundle (include pcap, proxy logs, kv audit) — due EOD today.
- Jess: rollback coordination + canary verification notes — due in 30m.
- Lia: customer communication (summary + ask for any retained PII exposures) — ongoing.
- Eng Runtime (eng_runtime_pm): create PR for route-resolver fixes and test harness for overlapping binds — assignable this sprint.

jess_prod_oncall: Canary looks green for 15m. No new ambiguous logs. I'll keep the rollback staged until ops says widen.

omar_sre: Evidence bundle collected. Key counts: ~12 requests matched with wrong tenant headers, window 13:04:08–13:07:02. Pcap shows no external exfil — traffic stayed within dataplane. Preparing sanitized attach for support.

lia_support: Peregrine's security asks: can you confirm whether any customer PII was included in the mismatched responses? They will share sample payloads. I'll block on Omar's evidence but flagging high priority.

omar_sre: Early look: responses included model output and metadata but not KV-store plaintext secrets. Still need to map keys to PII-sensitive records — continuing.

eng_runtime_pm: Noted; we'll prioritize key sensitivity mapping in the RCA. Also schedule a postmortem with Peregrine for tomorrow 10:00 PT.

ops_triage_lead: Handing off to night on-call. @jess_prod_oncall please capture the current state and action log in the incident tracker. If the canary re-fails, escalate to on-call SRE immediately.

jess_prod_oncall: Handoff summary posted in tracker: rollback rr-2026-03-14-81 -> rr-2026-03-14-80 performed at 13:06Z on proxies (proxy-7, proxy-9). Prefix-sanity guard applied for 60s. Evidence bundle in /incidents/peregrine/2543219876/. Currently canary stable 13:06–13:21Z. Open items: full key-sensitivity audit, RCA writeup, PR for resolver fix.

incident_bot: Incident marked: mitigated. Pager status -> degraded monitoring.

ops_triage_lead: Thanks team. Lia, keep Peregrine informed and schedule RCA review. Omar, attach sanitized evidence to the tracker. Eng Runtime please link PR when ready.

lia_support: Will do. Peregrine requested an export of affected request_ids and a concise timeline — sending now.

jess_prod_oncall: Passing to night: on-call is @night_sre. If anything reappears, notify pager, otherwise I'll sync tomorrow morning for RCA closure.

omar_sre: Uploaded bundle and next steps in tracker. Leaving monitoring alerts at high sensitivity for dp-phi-21.

eng_runtime_pm: Creating epic for route-resolver fixes and testcases. ETA for patch: 3 working days, will provide interim mitigation if needed.

incident_bot: Incident closed by jess_prod_oncall (mitigated).
